bull.b: Sustained, rapid Attruby revenue growth reflects durable commercial execution: strong uptake, expanding prescriber engagement, and effective patient identification. As the company scales sales and captures more of the treatable population, recurring product revenues provide a lasting revenue base to fund expansion and pipeline work.

Very high gross margins indicate attractive unit economics for marketed products and royalties. These margins increase the leverage of incremental sales to profit as commercialization scales, improving the path to sustainable operating profitability once fixed launch costs moderate and payers stabilize access.

Multiple late-stage NDAs and upcoming approvals markedly diversify future revenue streams beyond Attruby. Successful launches would create multi-product commercial footprint, reduce single-product risk, and leverage existing commercial infrastructure, making revenue growth more durable and less dependent on one asset.

bear.b: Large, persistent negative operating and free cash flow shows the company still consumes substantial cash to support launches and R&D. Even with recent financing, ongoing burn heightens reliance on external capital or asset monetization, which can pressure strategy, timing of launches, and long-term dilution risk if commercialization underperforms.

A sizable negative equity balance signals cumulative losses and prior financings that reduce balance-sheet flexibility. This structural deficit increases sensitivity to future funding terms, constrains strategic optionality, and elevates dilution or restrictive investor protections if additional capital is required to sustain multi-product launches.

The CARDIO-TTRansform failure weakens the case for combination strategies and leaves open comparative efficacy questions vs RNA knockdown competitors. Coupled with payer contract-driven net price erosion cited by peers, this structural uncertainty can limit long-term uptake, pricing power, and market share across ATTR and adjacent indications.
